sources.title: Historical assessment of agricultural drought impact in the Syrian Arab Republic (2021–2025)
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO portal summary of a technical assessment of drought conditions and affected agricultural areas during 2021–2025, published 1 September 2026.
sources.methodology: FAO describes satellite remote sensing and geospatial analysis of drought frequency, severity, duration and affected agricultural areas.
sources.limitations: Accessible portal summary gives national estimates but no named governorate-level hotspots or underlying detailed tables.

sources.title: Syrian Arab Republic Appeal: Humanitarian Action for Children 2026
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF's August 2026 revised annual appeal reports needs and displacement through 2026 and planned response targets.
sources.methodology: UNICEF operational appeal summarizing humanitarian needs, response priorities and planned agency targets.
sources.limitations: Operational needs and targets are not independent causal estimates or an evaluation of response outcomes.

sources.title: Syrian Arab Republic Humanitarian Situation Report No. 18 (End of Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: UNICEF operational reporting on the 2025 humanitarian situation, including early-2025 clashes and climate-related water stress.
sources.methodology: UNICEF annual operational reporting from monitoring and partner information.
sources.limitations: Operational reporting is not independent causal attribution; the PDF text was not rendered.

sources.title: FAO scales up irrigation rehabilitation to strengthen agricultural recovery and climate resilience in Aleppo
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO report dated 29 April 2025 on rehabilitation works at the West Maskanah Farm No. 9 irrigation scheme.
sources.methodology: FAO project report describing the rehabilitation scope and intended beneficiaries, drawing on assessments and community discussions.
sources.limitations: The page reports works and intended access, not independently measured household reach or resilience outcomes.

sources.title: FAO launches its emergency and recovery plan of action to restore agriculture in Syria
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: FAO's 19 March 2025 launch description of the proposed Emergency and Recovery Plan of Action for 2025–2027.
sources.methodology: FAO announcement summarizes its planned emergency, recovery, resilience and early-recovery package.
sources.limitations: This is a plan-launch page; proposed reach, activities and peace effects are intentions, not verified delivery or evaluated results.

sources.title: Syria Context Report
sources.temporal_coverage: FEWS NET context assessment dated 31 December 2025, including the post-December 2024 transition and conditions reported through 2025.
sources.methodology: Country context synthesis of conflict, livelihood, market, food-security and agroclimatic evidence with cited partner sources.
sources.limitations: The report synthesizes heterogeneous sources and identifies data gaps; its multi-driver framing does not quantify each driver's separate contribution.

claims.locator: Portal summary, paragraphs 2–4, beginning 'This assessment utilized satellite remote sensing'.
claims.paraphrase: FAO's retrospective geospatial assessment identifies rainfed croplands and grazing areas as especially drought-vulnerable, with many locations experiencing repeated one-to-two-month drought periods during 2021–2025.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: The accessible portal summary does not name the affected locations or estimate household-level losses.

claims.paraphrase: For 2025, FAO estimated that over 65% of both the human and livestock populations were potentially exposed to severe or extreme drought conditions.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: This is estimated potential exposure, not a count of people or animals who experienced a measured loss; the summary provides no local breakdown.

claims.locator: Country needs and strategy, 'Humanitarian needs' subsection, paragraph beginning 'Access to safe water'.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports that 10 million people cannot meet basic water needs and that drought-like conditions, erratic rainfall and flooding have exacerbated vulnerabilities across northern governorates, along the Euphrates and in coastal regions.
affected_groups: people unable to meet basic water needs
claims.limitations: UNICEF gives a national water-access estimate; the appeal does not disaggregate the 10 million by named governorate or hazard.

claims.locator: Country needs and strategy, 'Humanitarian needs' subsection, paragraph beginning 'Displacements in the Syrian Arab Republic'.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF reports that renewed violence in Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa and Al-Hasakeh displaced more than 170,000 people in early 2026; it also reports 187,000 displaced after the July 2025 As-Sweida escalation and continuing pressure from returns.
claims.limitations: These are UNICEF-reported displacement counts for specified episodes, not current governorate-level displacement stocks or climate-linked estimates.

claims.locator: 'Humanitarian Situation' section, paragraph on climate-induced shocks and water scarcity.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF says 2025 heatwaves, winter conditions and erratic rainfall heightened water scarcity and exacerbated the long-term impacts of conflict and water scarcity for 8.5 million people, including 1.8 million described as severely affected.
claims.limitations: Operational report; no independent attribution or governorate breakdown is provided.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF says climate-induced shocks heightened water scarcity and exacerbated long-term impacts of conflict and water scarcity for 8.5 million people; this is not an independent causal estimate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: 'Humanitarian Situation' section, paragraph on climate-induced shocks and water scarcity.

claims.locator: 'Humanitarian Situation' section, paragraph on early-2025 clashes around Tishreen Dam.
claims.paraphrase: UNICEF says early-2025 clashes around Tishreen Dam threatened electricity and water supplies for over 3.5 million people, before conditions eased after a March agreement.
affected_groups: people reliant on electricity and water services
claims.limitations: The report gives no service-loss duration or evidence of a climate-adaptation activity disrupted by conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Clashes around Tishreen Dam threatened electricity and water for over 3.5 million; conditions later eased after a March agreement.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: 'Humanitarian Situation' section, paragraph on early-2025 clashes around Tishreen Dam.

claims.locator: Article paragraphs on the West Maskanah–Farm No. 9 intervention and construction activities.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports rehabilitating the West Maskanah–Farm No. 9 irrigation scheme in Aleppo Governorate, with the stated aim of ensuring irrigation access for about 3,970 smallholder households across 3,645 hectares; works included canals, field distribution and drainage systems.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
Building Local Resilience in Syria project
claims.limitations: FAO reports completed rehabilitation and intended access; the page does not verify household uptake, crop outcomes or resilience effects.

claims.locator: 'FAO ERPA 2025–2027: A Comprehensive Integrated Plan', planned outcomes 2–4 and landmine/UXO paragraph.
claims.paraphrase: FAO's 2025–2027 plan proposes irrigation and drainage rehabilitation, climate-smart practices and resource management, livelihood support for smallholders including IDPs and host communities, and clearance of mines and unexploded ordnance from farming land.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: These are announced plan activities for 2025–2027; the launch page does not verify delivery or land returned to cultivation.

claims.locator: Opening plan rationale, paragraph beginning 'A thriving agriculture sector'.
claims.paraphrase: FAO's ERPA announcement presents stronger agriculture as a proposed route to community resilience and peace by reducing competition over scarce resources.
institutions: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
claims.limitations: This is plan rationale and stated intent, not an evaluated climate-conflict effect or evidence that competition caused violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO states that a thriving agriculture sector is intended to promote peace by reducing competition over scarce resources; the statement is prospective plan rationale, not a measured outcome.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Opening plan rationale, paragraph beginning 'A thriving agriculture sector'.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, final paragraph; 'Food Security and Nutrition Context', paragraph beginning 'Key areas of concern'.
claims.paraphrase: FEWS NET's December 2025 context report lists Aleppo, Daraa, Deir ez-Zor, Al-Hasakah, Homs, Idlib, Ar-Raqqa and Rural Damascus as food-security areas of concern, and identifies recurrent drought, low Euphrates levels, displacement, insecurity and economic shocks among drivers of poor households' acute food insecurity.
claims.limitations: This is a dated multi-source context synthesis; it identifies concurrent drivers but does not estimate their separate causal contributions by governorate.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FEWS NET identifies recurrent drought and hydrological drought alongside displacement, insecurity and economic shocks as key drivers of acute food insecurity among poor households; it does not attribute insecurity to drought.

search_audit.query: Syria 2025 2026 drought climate vulnerability governorates subnational water agriculture FAO UNICEF report
search_audit.outcome: Found an FAO 2021–2025 satellite drought assessment and 2026 UNICEF needs summary, plus FEWS NET governorate-level food-security areas of concern; the accessible FAO summary does not name drought hotspots.

search_audit.query: Syria climate shocks drought conflict food insecurity water scarcity displacement explicit source stated relationship UNICEF FAO FEWS NET 2025
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF's end-2025 excerpt says climate shocks heightened water scarcity and exacerbated conflict impacts; FEWS NET lists drought, insecurity, displacement and economic shocks among food-insecurity drivers. FAO's 2025 plan proposes an agriculture-to-peace pathway through reducing resource competition. These are source statements, not independent causal findings; no source inspected attributes violence to climate.

search_audit.query: Syria conflict insecurity damage disrupted irrigation water infrastructure farming land mines climate adaptation recovery 2025 report
search_audit.outcome: UNICEF reports clashes threatened water and electricity at Tishreen Dam; FAO reports a planned mine/UXO clearance component and FEWS NET describes insecurity and displacement constraints on agriculture and markets. These sources show conflict-related service or livelihood constraints, but do not evaluate a specific adaptation programme being blocked by violence.

search_audit.query: Syria Aleppo West Maskanah irrigation resilience climate adaptation community programme FAO 2025 outcomes
search_audit.outcome: Found FAO's reported completed West Maskanah Farm No. 9 rehabilitation and a national 2025–2027 recovery-plan design with proposed climate-smart agriculture and resource-safety activities. Reported works are not independently evaluated outcomes; the national plan remains a plan announcement.

gaps: The accessible FAO drought-assessment portal summary gives national exposure estimates but no named governorate-level hotspot results or detailed underlying tables.

The UNICEF end-2025 PDF was not rendered by the web reader; only continuous official excerpts were available. Its report-stated climate/conflict compounding relationship is not independent causal attribution.
No inspected source establishes that climate change or drought caused violence in Syria, or quantifies a climate-to-conflict pathway at a named locality.

Conflict-related threats to essential infrastructure and planned UXO clearance were documented, but no inspected source evaluates violence preventing a named climate-adaptation project from being delivered.

FAO's West Maskanah page reports rehabilitation and intended coverage but no follow-up data on water delivered, beneficiary uptake, crop yields or household resilience; the national FAO ERPA is an announced plan rather than an evaluated outcome.
FEWS NET's December 2025 report is a multi-source context synthesis with heterogeneous input data; dated 2025/26 forecasts were excluded rather than treated as current outcomes.
